articles.title: Cucumber Company becomes Smtn else
articles.summary: At the start of Season 8 (autumn 2022) Cucumber Company was archived and renamed 'Smtn else' — as Gang of Fools left and Paladins United, The Simple Ones and TerraLune joined — then renamed 'smtn elf' for Christmas 2022 and never changed back.
articles.body:
At the start of guild Season 8, in the autumn of 2022, [[Cucumber Company]] — the fourteen-guild super-alliance of the 2022 realignment — changed its name. "Cucumber was archived. The new alliance name is called Smtn else," recorded Titans Valor's newsletter, the Titan Times, which in the same breath noted that Gang of Fools had "left and betrayed the alliance" and welcomed three new members: [[Paladins United]], [[The Simple Ones]] and TerraLune.

The chronicle approximates the transition to the season boundary, around 24 Sep 2022. The membership otherwise carried over — the Titan Times frames it as a rename, not a reformation.

## The second rename

For Christmas 2022 "Smtn else" became "smtn elf" — and was never renamed back. The Christmas rename itself survives only in oral testimony, but the resulting name is corroborated in writing by 17 Feb 2023, when a forum post called [[smtn-elf|smtn elf]] "unquestionably the greatest super-alliance of 2023."

Under that accidental permanent name the alliance dominated the map into 2023, until [[The Avocado split]] and [[smtn-elf-fades-away|its quiet dissolution]] that summer.

## Sources

- Titan Times vol. 6 (12 Oct 2022 — the archiving, the betrayal, the three joins)
- Cameron oral history (testimony — the Christmas rename)
- Wynncraft forums thread 306790 (17 Feb 2023 — earliest written "smtn elf")

articles.title: First machine-recorded alliances
articles.summary: The four in-game ally events of June 2026, captured by Sequoia's open-source mod: the first records of guild relationships in Wynncraft produced by software rather than written down by a person. They document registrations in the game's ally system, a relationship used chiefly to permit allied guilds to run guild raids together, and are not evidence of political alliances.

infobox.label: What the records are
infobox.value: In-game ally registrations — a game-mechanical status used chiefly to permit joint guild raids

infobox.label: What they are not

articles.body:
The first machine-recorded alliances are the four in-game ally events of June 2026 captured by [[Sequoia]]'s open-source mod — the first records of guild relationships in Wynncraft produced by software rather than by a person writing them down.

What they record is a registration in Wynncraft's in-game ally system: a game-mechanical status that sets the tax rate between two guilds' territories and, from 2026, lets them run guild raids together. It is not a political alliance. Guilds registered as in-game allies may be rivals, and may have recently fought each other, so these records cannot be read as blocs, pacts or reconciliations.

## Background

Wynncraft's in-game ally system has existed since version 1.20 (20 January 2021 — see [[the-diplomacy-update]]). Setting another guild as an ally applies the ally tax rate on that guild's territories and, from 2026, permits joint guild raids; it requires no political alignment and is neither announced nor explained anywhere outside the game.

The game's official API exposes no alliance field (verified 2 September 2026), so for the system's first five years its state was invisible outside the client. The political alliances of the same period survived only in forum posts like [[the-forum-megalist|the megalist]] — and after the last public roster in June 2022, mostly not at all. Through [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]], alliance history went dark.

## The records

On 12 June 2026, Sequoia's mod (SequoiaWynncraft/Sequoia-mod, commit 69fb472) added parsing for the in-game 'formed/revoked an alliance with' chat lines, and its test fixtures quote the captured broadcasts verbatim:

- Sequoia formed an alliance with Silk Road
- Anime Lovers revoked the alliance with Sequoia
- [[GazTheCat]], Sequoia's owner, revoked the alliance with Chiefs Of Corkus
- Tannslee formed an alliance with Radiant Roses

Each line records an ally registration being created or cancelled, and nothing beyond that about the relations between the guilds involved. The guilds named — Silk Road, Anime Lovers, Chiefs Of Corkus and Radiant Roses — were all live on the official API in September 2026.

Allied guilds gained the ability to run guild raids together in 2026: the chronicle database dates the change to version 2.2.2 (10 July 2026), while the wiki's changelogs attribute it to version 2.2.1 (12 June 2026), a conflict noted at [[the-diplomacy-update|The Diplomacy update]]. That capability is the system's principal use. From 30 July 2026 (mod commit 8b27368, Modrinth 1.8.0 changelog) the mod began auto-snapshotting the in-game Diplomacy menu — up to 16 allies — to Sequoia's private backend: a growing machine-readable record of ally registrations, though not a publicly accessible one.

## Significance and limits

The June 2026 events are the first guild-relationship records in Wynncraft produced without a human chronicler: dated, verbatim and generated by the game itself. The snapshotting added in July 2026 extends that to a guild's whole ally list rather than to individual changes, making the state of the system reconstructable rather than only its transitions.

The scope of the evidence is narrow. It shows which guilds were registered as one another's in-game allies; it does not record why a registration was made, and it does not establish that the guilds named were politically aligned or acting together in a war. The alliances that decided the wars of the private-diplomacy era — including the ongoing [[aequitas-sequoia-war|Aequitas-Sequoia war]] — were made in private Discords, and nothing in the machine record recovers them.

## Sources

- SequoiaWynncraft/Sequoia-mod, commit 69fb472 (12 Jun 2026) — chat-line parser and test fixtures quoting the four events
- SequoiaWynncraft/Sequoia-mod, commit 8b27368 + Modrinth 1.8.0 changelog (30 Jul 2026) — Diplomacy-menu snapshotting
- Wynncraft version history (ally system in 1.20, 20 Jan 2021; Guild Raids for allies in 2.2.2, 10 Jul 2026)
- Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guild War': ally taxation
- Official Wynncraft API, v3/guild (no alliance field; verified 2 Sep 2026)

articles.title: History of Wynncraft guild warfare
articles.summary: A survey of twelve years of Wynncraft guild warfare, 2014–2026: from the first guilds and the HackForums dominance through the mega-alliances, the Great Collapse and the super-alliances, to the private-diplomacy wars whose alliances were never published.

infobox.label: Primary sources
infobox.value: [[the-forum-megalist|The forum megalist]], [[Titan Times]], territory_exchanges map data

articles.body:
{{map:2018-06-01|The territory map in the Federation era}}

Guild warfare — the contest for the territory map of the Wynn provinces — is nearly as old as Wynncraft's guilds themselves, introduced in [[the-guild-update|the Guild Update]] of December 2014. Twelve years of it divide into six eras, and the quality of the record divides with them: the earliest years survive only in forum accounts, a continuous territory-exchange log begins in January 2018, and from 2026 the game itself records guild ally registrations — a game-mechanical relationship, not a political one (see [[territory-warfare|Territory warfare]] for the mechanics and the methodology).

## The early powers (2014–2017)

The [[early-guild-era|early guild era]] produced the first alliances — above all [[Valkyrie]], founded in June 2015 by Kingdom of Foxes and [[Imperial]] and destined to outlive everything around it — and the first hegemon: [[HackForums]], which in September 2016 held 146 of roughly 332 territories, ahead of the otherwise-unrecorded [[Libertas]]. Hax's mega-alliance peaked near 350 territories in 2017 before falling; the [[Coalition]] rose in its place, taking the whole map by Christmas 2017.

## The age of the mega-alliances (2018–2019)

In February 2018 the Coalition split, and the [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]] between it and [[Alliance Alliance]] birthed the [[the-federation|Federation]] under [[Drew1011]]. The Federation [[the-wipe-of-hackforums|wiped HackForums' 111 territories in under 12 hours]], grew to some 40 guilds (with the [[Aesir Pact]] inside it), and held the entire map for 8 months and 25 days — then [[the-federation-dies|cascaded apart in a single day]] on 10 November 2018 (the [[federation-era|Federation era]]). What followed was churn: in thirteen months [[SOL]], [[Luna]], [[Terra]], the [[Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] and [[Horologium]] each rose and collapsed, punctuated by the treaties of Rodoroc and Ternaves and Luna's brief total map control ([[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]]).

## Artemis, Goose and the Great Collapse (2020–2021)

[[Artemis]] emerged from 2019 as map holder and transformed across 2020 — its founders [[Paladins United]] and Imperial ending up in the opposing coalition that became [[Goose]]. The [[goose-artemis-war|Goose–Artemis war]] consumed the map until 11 May 2021, when both alliances died on the same day — [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]] — while community alliances ([[Hestia]], [[Niflheim]], the [[Empire of Nemract]]) ran alongside the fighting and [[Profession Heaven]] was jointly protected as a neutral guild ([[artemis-goose-era|the Artemis–Goose era]]).

## Realignment and the super-alliances (2021–2023)

From the Collapse rose [[Valhalla]] and [[Khaos]], at war from their first day ([[valhalla-khaos-war|Valhalla–Khaos war]]); [[Vanir]] inherited Valhalla's side and lived twenty days. The 2022 realignment merged both worlds into [[Cucumber Company]] — whose 14-guild roster, posted to [[the-forum-megalist|the forum megalist]] in June 2022, was the last public alliance roster ever — renamed [[smtn elf]] by Christmas. In June 2023 [[The Aquarium]] and [[Avicia]] walked out ([[the-avocado-split|the Avocado split]]) and the super-alliance faded without an obituary ([[the-realignment-era|the realignment era]]).

## The private diplomacy era (2023–2026)

Since then, diplomacy has lived in private Discords, and only the map attests the wars: the [[avicia-sequoia-war|Avicia–Sequoia war]], the [[idiot-co-aquarium-war|Idiot Co–Aquarium war]] (the biggest since 2021), [[the-long-raid|the Long Raid]], the record-setting [[aequitas-avicia-war|Aequitas–Avicia war]] of 2025, the 2026 fall of Profession Heaven's neutrality, and the ongoing [[aequitas-sequoia-war|Aequitas–Sequoia war]] against seven-season champion [[Sequoia]]. In June 2026 a machine record appeared, though not of diplomacy: Sequoia's client mod began capturing the game's in-game ally broadcasts ([[first-machine-recorded-alliances|the first machine-recorded alliances]]), a registration used chiefly to permit allied guilds to run guild raids together ([[the-diplomacy-update|The Diplomacy update]]). Who was allied with whom, and why, remains unpublished ([[private-diplomacy-era|the private diplomacy era]]).

## Reading this history

The record behind these articles: the [[the-forum-megalist|forum megalist]] (the community's public alliance list, 2020–2022), [[Titan Times]] (Titans Valor's newsletter, 2022–2025), the game updates that reshaped warring ([[the-guild-update|Guild]], [[the-economy-update|Economy]], [[guild-seasons|Seasons]], [[the-diplomacy-update|Diplomacy]]), and continuous territory-exchange analysis whose limits are explained in [[territory-warfare|Territory warfare]].

## Sources

- The chronicle database (22 alliances, 36 events) and its cited forum threads, in particular 237070, 278112, 279337 and 265297
- Titan Times vols. 1–21 (May 2022 – Nov 2025)
- pre2018-territory-snapshots.json (2016–2019 leaderboard captures)
- territory_exchanges map-data analysis (Jan 2018 – present)
- Official Wynncraft Wiki (update names and dates)

articles.title: Luna gains full map control
articles.summary: After fending off an attack on Kingdom Foxes, Luna wiped every guild but Avicia; Avicia joined on 17 Jul 2019 and Luna held the entire map — a control that lasted until Terra took it on 8 Sep 2019.
articles.body:
{{map:2019-07-17|The map under Luna's control}}

In July 2019 [[Luna]] reached its peak. [[Kingdom Foxes]] had joined on 8 Jul, ending [[luna-s-war-on-kingdom-foxes|five months of war]]; Luna then fended off an attack on its newest member and wiped every remaining guild from the map except [[Avicia]]. On 17 Jul 2019 Avicia joined the alliance, and Luna held the entire map.

It was the third full-map hold in the recorded era, after the [[coalition|Coalition]]'s dominance from Christmas 2017 and [[the-federation|The Federation]]'s eight months and twenty-five days across 2018. Luna's proved the briefest: [[emorians-and-avicia-revolt|Emorians and Avicia revolted]] on 29 Aug after a leadership dispute, [[Terra]] formed in the chaos on 30 Aug, and on 8 Sep 2019 — after The Simple Ones defected — Terra took the map ([[Luna-Terra war]]). Luna had held it for 53 days.

At its height the alliance counted roughly ten guilds, including [[Imperial]], [[Emorians]], Blacklisted, BuildCraftia, [[The Simple Ones]], Kingdom Foxes, Caeruleum Order and Avicia.

## Sources

- community Timeline document (the Avicia join and full-map control, 17 Jul 2019)
- territory_exchanges map-data analysis (the July wipe; the 8 Sep 2019 loss of control)

articles.title: Profession Heaven neutrality
articles.summary: On 25 Jan 2021 Profession Heaven was granted neutral status, protected by both Goose and Artemis, and given Silent Expanse territory as a public profession-XP guild — an arrangement that held for over five years.
articles.body:
On 25 Jan 2021, in the middle of the [[Goose-Artemis war]], [[Profession Heaven]] was granted neutral status — protected by both warring alliances at once — and given territory in the Silent Expanse to operate as a public profession-XP guild. Its first recorded territory exchange falls on that same day.

The arrangement was unique in the record: a guild holding land on a contested map by the joint consent of both sides of a map-wide war.

## A five-year peace

The neutrality outlived its guarantors. When Goose and Artemis collapsed together on 11 May 2021 ([[The Great Collapse]]), protection carried over to their successors. Profession Heaven eventually joined the blocs outright, appearing on [[Cucumber Company]]'s final public roster of 26 Jun 2022 and remaining through the rename into [[smtn-elf|smtn elf]] until that alliance's end in mid-2023 — while its protected, neutral character as a public XP guild persisted.

The arrangement held until 25 May 2026, when KongoBoys — itself a former Cucumber Company ally — began the sustained campaign that [[fall-of-profession-heaven-s-neutrality|ended the neutrality]] after more than five years.

## Sources

- community Timeline document (the 25 Jan 2021 grant and joint protection)
- territory_exchanges map-data analysis (first exchange on the grant date)
- the forum megalist, thread 278112 p8 (the 26 Jun 2022 Cucumber Company roster)

articles.title: Territory warfare
articles.summary: How Wynncraft guild wars actually work — territories, wars before and after the 1.20 rework, seasons, FFA hotspots and ally territory-trading — and why raw exchange volume is not evidence of war.
articles.body:
Wynncraft's provinces are divided into territories that guilds capture and hold. Territory warfare has existed since [[the-guild-update|the Guild Update]] of December 2014, in two mechanical epochs.

## The two war systems

In the original system (2014–2021), wars spawned waves of mobs on dedicated war servers and territories generated XP for their holders. Version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021) rebuilt it: attacking now costs guild emeralds and is resolved by defeating the territory's war tower; territories produce resources moved along trade routes, can be taxed (including a separate ally tax), and support a headquarters whose strength scales with connected holdings. Patch 1.20.3 (5 July 2021) added [[guild-seasons|guild seasons]] — Season Rating earned by holding and attacking territories, with resets and rewards every season — which turned holding land into a scheduled competition.

## Reading the exchange record

The chronicle's map-data analysis rests on the territory_exchanges log (continuous since 3 January 2018). Its central methodological rule: **exchange volume is not war**. Two phenomena generate enormous exchange counts in peacetime:

- **FFA hotspots** — clusters that churn perpetually regardless of politics, such as Detlas, the Hive, Lava Lake, Factory Entrance and the Emerald Trail, joined in 2020–21 by the Silent Expanse. Fighting concentrated on these territories is noise, not campaign.
- **Ally territory-trading** — from the 1.20 era, allied guilds mass-trade territories for XP and SR, producing near-symmetric exchange counts (Avicia and Emorians once traded roughly 5,000 captures each way while allied).

A real war instead shows spread and asymmetry: sustained fighting across 100+ territories with a low share on FFA clusters. The chronicle therefore counts 'quiet-territory exchanges' — captures outside the FFA hotspots — when dating and sizing wars, and treats bloc rosters inferred from co-belligerence as labeled inference, never as attested fact. The [[goose-artemis-war|Goose]] roster episode, where map inference initially contradicted the written record, is the standing cautionary tale.

## Sources

- Official Wynncraft Wiki: 'Guilds', 'Guild War', 'Version 1.20', version history
- Wynncraft forums thread 292974 (1.20.3 changelog)
- Chronicle draft methodology notes (chronicle-alliances-draft-2018-2021.json; chronicle-research-notes-2020-2026.md): FFA filtering, ally-trading detection, war criteria

articles.title: The forum megalist
articles.summary: Wynncraft forums thread 278112, created and maintained by Sg_Voltage from 29 November 2020: the community-maintained list of guilds and alliances. Its posts of December 2020 - June 2022 are the backbone of the attested alliance record; its alliance section was deleted on 7 July 2022, ending public alliance rosters.
articles.body:
The 'megalist' is Wynncraft forums thread 278112, a community-maintained listing of guilds and their alliances. Between December 2020 and June 2022 it was the only public, dated record of who was allied with whom - and nearly every attested alliance roster of the [[artemis-goose-era|Artemis-Goose]] and [[the-realignment-era|realignment]] eras traces to one of its posts.

## Authorship

The thread was created on 29 November 2020 by [[sg-voltage|Sg_Voltage]], who maintained it for years afterwards. Earlier chronicle notes credited the megalist to 'Pally'; that is wrong. Pally - [[paladinsorcerer|PaladinSorcerer]] of [[Titans Valor]] - was a reader, and the author of the thread's single most load-bearing alliance attestation, but never its maintainer. Sg_Voltage's own guild affiliation is unknown: the forum profile shown in the 4 July 2021 Wayback capture displays a CHAMPION rank and no guild field at all.

The opening post set out the project - 'I've assembled a list of every* guild which is currently recruiting along with some important stats for each ... My goal is to be able to make sure every guild gets the chance to shine' - and the listing itself lived in a Google Sheet edited by the guilds themselves: 'If you're a high ranking member of a guild and want to see your guild added or want to make changes, send me a message with your Gmail and I'll give you editing permission.' One of the sheet's columns was Alliances - 'Some guilds are in alliances for warring, this is where they're listed' - and that column is why the thread matters to guild history. After Sg_Voltage was asked whether he intended to update it weekly, forum administrator colin350 pinned the thread on 17 January 2021.

## Landmark posts

Its landmark entries include: the 2 December 2020 post by Pally (post #10) recording that 'ANO is apart of the alliances Hestia (a community alliance between ANO, ESI, LXA, and PUN) and Artemis (war alliance) made up of all the current massive land holding guilds on the map' - the founding attestation for both [[Hestia]] and [[Artemis]]; two posts on the morning of 19 January 2021, 99loulou999's 'TNR (TNI and TNA) are part of Goose' and Lev98bug's 'Eden is in Goose if you could add that', the earliest recorded uses of the name [[Goose]], to which Sg_Voltage replied 'Just want to drop in and say that I'm a huge fan of the name'; the 1 February 2021 side-switch report by urbymine ('BNU(IBT), SHY and TNL are all goose now'); the 25 May 2021 post recording the [[Valhalla]]/[[Khaos]] renames after [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]]; Pally's six-guild Hestia roster of 6 June 2021; the 7 July 2021 [[Niflheim]] roster; and the 26 June 2022 post giving [[Cucumber Company]]'s full 14-guild roster - the last public alliance roster ever posted anywhere.

## The deletion

Twelve days later, on 7 July 2022, the thread's alliance section was deleted. Replying to the Cucumber Company roster in post #161, Sg_Voltage first explained that 'for alliance information, it's supposed to be updated by the guilds themselves, I noticed it was out of date so I just moved it to the side. I don't care to follow guild drama', then added: 'You know what, on second thought I'm just going to delete that section. If it's not updated regularly it's not really useful anyways.' The deletion marks the boundary between the public record and [[private-diplomacy-era|the private diplomacy era]]: no alliance roster has been published since.

The thread itself outlived its alliance column. Sg_Voltage reported the sheet being flagged by Google in January 2023 and was still fielding update requests that March, and readers were still posting to it in 2025. The underlying Google Sheet was never captured by any web archive, so the Valhalla- and Khaos-era rosters it once held are gone from the public web; the thread's posts survive partly through Wayback Machine snapshots.

## Sources

- Wynncraft forums thread 278112, opening post and posts of 2 Dec 2020 (p1, #8 and #10, Pally), 14-17 Jan 2021 (p4, #64-67, the pinning), 19 Jan 2021 (p4, #71-73), 1 Feb 2021 (p4, #76, urbymine), 25 May 2021 (p7), 6 Jun 2021 (p7, Pally's Hestia roster), 7 Jul 2021 (p8, #146), 26 Jun 2022 (p8, #160) and 7 Jul 2022 (p9, #161, the deletion)
- Wayback Machine snapshots of the thread (2021-07-04, 2021-11-28, 2022-05-17, 2022-09-15); the 2021-07-04 capture preserves Sg_Voltage's and Pally's forum profiles and the alliance column description
- Chronicle research notes (2020-2026): authorship correction and the lost Google Sheet

articles.title: Titan Times
articles.summary: Titans Valor's guild newsletter, volumes 1-21 (May 2022 - May 2026): the most important primary source for alliance history after the forum megalist's deletion, documenting Cucumber Company, smtn elf, Hestia's decline and Adonis before turning inward after 2023.

infobox.label: Writers/editors
infobox.value: bitesizedbee4 ('Bee'), GebutterteWurst ('Geb'), Snazz, Aezuh, C0rupted, Talkair, l1npengtul

articles.body:
Titan Times is the newsletter of the guild [[Titans Valor]] [ANO]. Twenty-one volumes were published between 8 May 2022 and 18 May 2026 (with a gap between vol. 11 of 25 May 2023 and vol. 12 of 20 February 2024), hosted at titansvalor.org/news, with the first thirteen volumes mirrored at titantimes.github.io. After [[the-forum-megalist|the forum megalist]]'s alliance section was deleted in July 2022, Titan Times became the only regularly published, dated account of alliance affairs - the key primary source for the late [[the-realignment-era|realignment era]].

The masthead changed hands twice. The founding writer and editor was bitesizedbee4 ('Bee'), who carried vols. 1 to 10 (8 May 2022 - 23 Apr 2023); GebutterteWurst ('Geb'), an ANO Councilor, joined as co-editor from vol. 7 (16 Dec 2022); Snazz wrote the recent-happenings column; Aezuh handled visuals and publishing and was still being thanked for reviewing and posting the team's work in vol. 20; a member credited only as Andrew gave technical support in vol. 2; and karapandza appeared as a guest writer in vols. 10 and 11. C0rupted introduced himself as 'the new writer' in vol. 12 (Feb 2024) and remained on the team through vol. 21. From vol. 16 (Nov 2024) Talkair became the lead voice, credited in vol. 20 with 'not only writing but organising Titan Times for 5 whole editions', with Lamplesspost writing the main-stage interviews from vol. 17. Vol. 21 (18 May 2026) announced another change: l1npengtul took over as Editor-in-Chief, alongside Talkair, DragonZftw and C0rupted, promising a quarterly schedule tied to the start of each guild season from vol. 22 onward.

Its most important records are concentrated in the first ten volumes: vol. 1 (8 May 2022) dates [[Cucumber Company]]'s formation to guild Season 5 ('our first season being a part of the new Cucumber Company war alliance') and the founding of [[Adonis]] as [[Hestia]] declined; vol. 3 (12 Jun 2022) records IceBlue Team's exit, Gang of Fools' arrival and [[Avicia]] joining Adonis; vol. 6 (12 Oct 2022) preserves the pivotal rename - 'Cucumber was archived. The new alliance name is called Smtn else' - along with Gang of Fools' betrayal and the accession of [[Paladins United]], [[The Simple Ones]] and TerraLune to what became [[smtn elf]]; vol. 9 (25 Mar 2023) records busted moments joining mid-season and Nefarious Ravens leaving 'on account of the guild disbanding'; vols. 12-13 (Feb-Mar 2024) attest Adonis still active.

After that the newsletter turns inward. Vols. 14-21 (2024-2026) cover guild events, the Spirit and Brilliance cabinets, dungeon and lore criticism, and ANO's internal Ocean Trials war rankings, but name no alliance at all - a documentary silence that matches [[private-diplomacy-era|the private diplomacy era]] rather than contradicting it. What they do preserve is ANO's own record: the guild reaching level 105 in mid-2024 (vol. 15), its season placings, and, in vol. 20 (23 Nov 2025), an interview with guild leader Calluum that is the only public account of ANO's leadership succession.

The newsletter's ecosystem also left machine traces: Titans Valor's Discord bot (github.com/titantimes/valor) consumed a shared ANO/AVO alliance-claims feed between April and December 2022 - infrastructure-level corroboration of the Cucumber-era alliance. That bot is not the work of [[motoki317]], whom earlier chronicle notes wrongly credited with it: motoki317 wrote moto-bot (github.com/motoki317/moto-bot), a separate Java Wynncraft utility bot with its own player-tracking commands, archived read-only on 27 January 2024. Nothing links motoki317 to Titans Valor.

## Sources

- Titan Times vols. 1-21: vols. 1-13 at titantimes.github.io, vols. 14-21 at titansvalor.org/news
- Vol. 1 (8 May 2022), vol. 3 (12 Jun 2022), vol. 6 (12 Oct 2022), vol. 9 (25 Mar 2023), vols. 12-13 (20 Feb and 22 Mar 2024): the alliance record
- Vol. 15 (5 Aug 2024), vol. 20 (23 Nov 2025) and vol. 21 (18 May 2026): guild level 105, the Calluum interview, the masthead handover to l1npengtul
- github.com/titantimes/valor (the 2022 alliance-claims feed) and github.com/motoki317/moto-bot (the separate, unrelated bot)
- Chronicle research notes (2020-2026), addendum 2 and the motoki317 correction

articles.title: Treaty of Damask
articles.summary: Signed 21 May 2021 by Nefarious Ravens and The Simple Ones, ten days after the Great Collapse; under it Nefarious Ravens declared independence.
articles.body:
The Treaty of Damask was signed on 21 May 2021 by Nefarious Ravens and [[The Simple Ones]]; under it, Nefarious Ravens declared independence. The treaty's terms beyond that declaration are unrecorded.

## Context

It was concluded ten days after [[The Great Collapse]] of 11 May 2021, in which [[Goose]] and [[Artemis]] fell on the same day and the map's guilds re-sorted themselves into [[Valhalla]] and [[Khaos]]. The Simple Ones had joined Valhalla at its founding; the treaty fixed Nefarious Ravens' position outside the new blocs as the [[Valhalla-Khaos war]] began.

## Legacy

Nefarious Ravens' independence lasted half a year. It was invited into [[Vanir]], Valhalla's successor, on 1 Dec 2021 — and was one of the four guilds whose departure [[vanir-collapses|collapsed Vanir]] seventeen days later. It went on to join [[Cucumber Company]] in the 2022 realignment, remaining through the rename into [[smtn-elf|smtn elf]] until the guild disbanded in March 2023.

## Sources

- community Timeline document (signatories, date, and the independence declaration)
- Titan Times vol. 9 (25 Mar 2023 — Nefarious Ravens leaving smtn elf "on account of the guild disbanding")

articles.title: Treaty of Rodoroc
articles.summary: A peace treaty between Kingdom Foxes and DiamondDeities, signed earlier and taking effect on 2 Mar 2019, during the SOL–Luna era.
articles.body:
The Treaty of Rodoroc was a peace treaty between [[Kingdom Foxes]] and [[DiamondDeities]], taking effect on 2 Mar 2019. The community Timeline document records that it had been signed earlier; the signing date itself is unrecorded, and no text of the treaty survives.

## Context

The treaty belongs to the fractured landscape after the Federation's fall. DiamondDeities was then part of [[sol|SOL]], the bloc [[Luna]] had been formed to counter two weeks earlier, while Kingdom Foxes stood alone, fighting [[luna-s-war-on-kingdom-foxes|a five-month war against Luna]]. The peace is consistent with an earlier arrangement between the two guilds recorded in the community guild-timeline image: a late-2018 deal to share the Molten Heights. Rodoroc, the treaty's namesake, is the dwarven capital of that region.

## Legacy

The record shows the peace holding: the two guilds went on to fight on the same side in [[Terra]] (September 2019) and the [[Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] that autumn, before [[diamonddeities-disbanded|DiamondDeities was disbanded]] in January 2020.

## Sources

- community Timeline document (parties and the 2 Mar 2019 effective date)
- community guild-timeline image (imgur seklYAQ, via forums thread 265297 — the late-2018 Molten Heights arrangement)

articles.title: Treaty of Ternaves
articles.summary: Signed 6 Jul 2019 by Kingdom Foxes, The Simple Ones and ThisIsMurica, splitting the territory of the dissolved Celestial Tigers — and clearing the way for Kingdom Foxes to join Luna two days later.
articles.body:
The Treaty of Ternaves was signed on 6 Jul 2019 by [[Kingdom Foxes]], [[The Simple Ones]] and ThisIsMurica, dividing the territory of the dissolved guild Celestial Tigers among the three. Nothing else about Celestial Tigers — its history, its size, or the circumstances of its dissolution — survives in the corpus.

## Context and consequence

At signing, The Simple Ones and ThisIsMurica were both members of [[Luna]], while Kingdom Foxes had been at war with that alliance since its second day of existence ([[luna-s-war-on-kingdom-foxes|Luna's war on Kingdom Foxes]], from 15 Feb 2019). The treaty proved to be the war's off-ramp: directly afterwards, on 8 Jul 2019, Kingdom Foxes joined Luna, ending nearly five months of fighting.

The consequences cascaded quickly. Within ten days the enlarged Luna wiped every remaining guild but [[Avicia]] and [[luna-gains-full-map-control|held the entire map]] — the peak from which the alliance would collapse two months later.

## Sources

- community Timeline document (signatories, date, and the Celestial Tigers division)

articles.title: The Artemis-Goose era
articles.summary: From the disbanding of DiamondDeities in January 2020 to the Great Collapse of 11 May 2021: Artemis held the map, its own founders drifted into the opposition that became Goose, and both alliances died on the same day. It is also the era in which the community began writing its own record down.
articles.body:
{{map:2021-02-01|The map at the height of the Goose-Artemis war}}

The Artemis-Goose era opens with the last aftershock of 2019 - [[Nitrogen2Oxygen]] disbanding [[DiamondDeities]] on 8 January 2020, which ended [[Horologium]] and birthed Lux Nova - and closes with the only day in the record on which both major alliances died at once.

## Artemis transformed

[[Artemis]], founded on 30 October 2019 by [[Imperial]], [[Paladins United]] and Caeruleum Order, became the era's map holder - but not with its founding roster. By March 2020 [[Kingdom Foxes]] was a member and [[ShadowFall]] held a leadership seat; by December 2020 a megalist post described Artemis as 'the war alliance made up of all the current massive land holding guilds', including [[Titans Valor]] - while founders Paladins United and Imperial had drifted out and appear on the opposing side. The exact join and leave dates of this transformation were never documented.

## The chroniclers

Almost everything known about this era's alliances was written by a handful of identifiable people, and their guild affiliations matter to how the claims should be weighed. [[the-forum-megalist|The megalist]] itself was created and maintained by [[sg-voltage|Sg_Voltage]], whose own guild is unknown - a neutral registrar. The December 2020 attestation of [[Hestia]] and Artemis was posted by [[paladinsorcerer|Pally]] of Titans Valor, a member of both. The 'Guild Moderators' thread that names the anti-Artemis coalition was written by Sheepn of Diablo [DXI], a coalition guild. The first written use of the name [[Goose]] came from 99loulou999 of The Dark Phoenix [TNI], with Eden's Lev98bug confirming his own guild's membership half an hour later. The 1 February 2021 side-switch report is [[urbymine]]'s, a former Chief of [[Avicia]]. The only [[Niflheim]] roster ever posted was written by HungHung of Avicia. And the era's most unusual document, a two-part illustrated roster of Goose, was drawn by [[drasalia|Drasalia]] of ChinaNumberOne. Every one of these writers was reporting on a bloc they belonged to, except Sg_Voltage.

## The social layer

Alongside the war blocs ran an unusually rich community-alliance layer: [[Hestia]] (formed ~mid-2020: Titans Valor, Empire of Sindria, Lux Nova, Paladins United, later Emorians and HackForums), [[Niflheim]] (Avicia, IceBlue Team, ShadowFall, TheNoLifes), the [[Empire of Nemract]] (a political union of [[The Simple Ones]] and Mystic Woods from 17 August 2020, complete with an empress and court titles), and the perennial [[Valkyrie]].

## The rise of Goose

In December 2020 an 'unnamed group of anti-Artemis guilds' - [[Avicia]], [[Emorians]], [[Eden]], Ultra Violet, Diablo, Bovemists, The Dark Phoenix, and ex-founders Paladins United and Imperial among them - erupted against the map holder: 913 quiet-territory exchanges that month, after months of skirmishing. By 19 January 2021 the coalition carried the name [[Goose]]. It grew through spring: 'BNU(IBT), SHY and TNL are all goose now', urbymine recorded on 1 February 2021 - ShadowFall switching sides from Artemis leadership - and by late March it had absorbed the future [[Khaos]] core ([[Aequitas]], WheresTheFinish, ChinaNumberOne, Fuzzy Spiders, Eden). Goose took map control as the [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]] ground on.

The new arrivals were not all new guilds. Aequitas had existed since November 2019 but only became publicly visible in this window: FrozenGalaxy opened its recruitment thread on 3 January 2021, added it to the megalist a fortnight later, and by 30 March it was one of the twelve guilds in Drasalia's fanart roster.

Mid-era, the game itself changed: version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021) rebuilt [[territory-warfare|territory warfare]] around war towers and a guild resource economy, and introduced the in-game ally system (see [[the-diplomacy-update|The Diplomacy update]]). The February 2021 argument over that rework, thread 286375, doubles as a war record: Eden's own members described crawling through Emorians territory held at medium and high defence, and the thread's Goose-side voices are named where the alliance rosters are not.

## Profession Heaven's neutrality

On 25 January 2021 the warring blocs jointly granted [[Profession Heaven]] neutral status as a public profession-XP guild, protected by both Goose and Artemis and given Silent Expanse territory - a protection honoured by successor alliances for over five years. The guild had been founded five days earlier by [[crokee|Crokee]]; the brokers of the pact itself are named in no surviving source.

## The Great Collapse

On 11 May 2021 Goose and Artemis both collapsed on the same day - [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]]. Thirteen guilds, including [[The Aquarium]], formed [[Valhalla]]; nine formed [[Khaos]]; and the [[the-realignment-era|realignment era]] began with the two new blocs already at war.

articles.title: Early guild era
articles.summary: The first period of Wynncraft guild warfare, from the introduction of guilds in December 2014 to the eve of the Coalition Civil War in early 2018. The era of Ordo Malleus and the Emperium of Wynn, of HackForums' map dominance, and of the rise of the Coalition — and the least documented period in the record.

infobox.label: State of the record
infobox.value: Forum accounts, a community timeline image, and two leaderboard captures; no exchange-level war data exists

articles.body:
{{map:2018-01-07|The earliest weeks of the recorded territory map, days after the era's close}}

The early guild era spans from the introduction of guilds in December 2014 to the fracturing of the [[Coalition]] in February 2018. It is the least documented period of Wynncraft guild warfare: the continuous territory-exchange log begins only on 3 January 2018, exchange-level pre-2018 war data was never archived anywhere public, and the era survives mainly through forum threads, a community-drawn timeline image, and two recovered captures of the guild leaderboard.

## The first guilds and the alliance layer (2014–2016)

Guilds and guild wars arrived together in [[the-guild-update|the Guild Update]] — version 1.13, the "Wynnter Update" of 22 December 2014. Within six months the era's most durable institution appeared: [[Valkyrie]], founded on 2 June 2015 by Kingdom of Foxes (later [[Kingdom Foxes]]) and [[Imperial]] "not for the purpose of war" and governed by an Electorate of guild masters. It would outlive every war alliance around it, remaining attested into 2022. It also set the constitutional template the period reused: internal affairs left to each guild, foreign policy pooled in a unanimous council of guild masters.

The war alliance of the same moment was [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]], the Order of the Hammer, created in November 2015 and remembered by [[drew1011|Drew1011]] in 2016 as "the greatest alliance to inhabit Wynn". Its one surviving roster, quoted from UltimateXeons' thread in February 2016, names twelve guilds bound by a single rule — "Don't attack the territories that ally guilds own" — and coordinating over Skype. It fell on 9 March 2016, in a veteran's account, "from the inside because of guilds fighting".

What followed Ordo's collapse was not another war bloc but a scatter of small community alliances, formed while one guild held most of the map and open warring paid poorly. [[halcyon|Halcyon]] (June 2016) paired ToastedPandas and Holders of LE in an "agreement for whenever help is needed"; [[seraphim|Seraphim]] (August 2016) declared itself "100% community based" with "no intention of actively providing support for guild wars"; [[aurelion|Aurelion]] (February 2017) gathered House of Sentinels, Hippies of Snuggles, The Dark Phoenix and Dragons Arise; and UltimateXeons' thread records a fourth, Lux Imperius. Membership overlapped freely — Seraphim's rules expressly allowed guilds to belong to several at once — and Holders of LE was in three of them within five months.

## The HackForums dominance

By 2016 the map belonged to [[HackForums]]. A Wayback Machine capture of the guild leaderboard from 23 September 2016 — one of only two structured territory datasets predating 2018 — shows Hax holding 146 of roughly 332 territories, ahead of [[Libertas]] with 60 and UltimateXeons with 53. Contemporaries were clear that Hax was not acting alone: "Hax has not been a one man army in ages," a poster objected in August 2016. "They work with Lir and Bla in order to hold territories." Adding Libertas' 60 and Blacklisted's 22 to Hax's 146 gives that bloc 228 of the map's 332 territories on the September 2016 capture, and Blacklisted's own thread stated the arrangement plainly: "We are allied with Libertas (Lir) and Hackforums (Hax)." The grouping is often called "Hax & Co" in later community memory; that name appears in no written source recovered so far.

Resentment was public and futile. "Right now there is 2 anti hax alliances," a Hax chief noted in June 2016, without naming either. In March 2017 a thread demanding that "Haxforums Should Be Limited On Territory Influence" charged that Hax held "100+ territories" by "taking advantage of the broken guild system" and "cheat the game with there control"; the thread's respondents, including Drew1011, uniformly rejected the idea of a cap — "Their success should not be limited just because other people are upset" — and one asked pointedly "are Lir, BLA, UXs somehow exempt?". Drew1011's diagnosis was that Hax's position was an artefact of the era rather than of strength: "The reason that Hax is able to hold so much is because, to put it simply, nobody is trying to challenge them." By May 2017 a forum thread title was asking why Hax had "MORE THAN 300 TERRITORIES", and a 2020 recollection put the peak "closer to 350", "when they owned the whole map".

## 2017: Emperium, War Syndicate and the Coalition

The [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]], founded on 21 April 2017 under Emperator [[nitrogen2oxygen|Nitrogen2Oxygen]], was the era's most elaborate institution: twelve member guilds with named leaders, a High Council of guild representatives, portfolio leaders for war, community and economy, judges whose word could not be over-ruled, and an oath for incoming members. It fell on 17 October 2017, the day after [[drew1011|Drew1011]] held the title of Emperator for a single day — a sequence no written source explains.

[[war-syndicate|War Syndicate]] was created on 17 July 2017 per the community timeline and is the era's largest documentary hole: no roster, no leader and no thread of its own survive. In October 2017 Kingdom Foxes, KingdomPhoenixes, Gilded Sparrows and House of Sentinels founded the [[Coalition]]. It took control of the Wynn province on 23 November 2017 and ended War Syndicate that December — "They wiped ws off the map on Christmas day", a veteran recalled in 2020, while another insisted the two blocs instead merged — entering 2018 with full map dominance.

## The state of the record

Nothing like a war log exists for these years. Archived 2015-era guild pages on wynncraft.com carry no territory counts, and 2016–2017 war events survive only as forum-thread imagery and written accounts. The two leaderboard captures — September 2016 and April 2018 — bracket the era; everything between them is narrative. How HackForums fell from roughly 350 territories to the 111 it held in February 2018 is recorded nowhere at all: no thread names the attackers, the dates or the sequence, and a 2020 participant called that collapse "probably the biggest event that happened in 2017". The era closed in mid-February 2018, when five guilds split from the Coalition over map disputes and opened the [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]], beginning the [[federation-era|Federation era]].

- Wynncraft forums thread 143392 ("Seraphim Alliance"), opening post (8 Aug 2016) and posts #7-#16 (9 Aug 2016) — the community-alliance terms, Ordo Malleus, "They work with Lir and Bla"

- Wynncraft forums thread 179383 ("Haxforums Should Be Limited On Territory Influence", 1 Mar 2017), posts #1, #5, #6 and #7

articles.title: The Federation era
articles.summary: The year 2018 in Wynncraft guild warfare: the Coalition Civil War, the rise of the Federation under Drew1011, its 8-month-and-25-day hold on the entire territory map, and its one-day collapse on 10 November 2018.

infobox.label: Key events
infobox.value: [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]], [[the-wipe-of-hackforums|The wipe of HackForums]], [[the-federation-dies|The Federation dies]]

articles.body:
{{map:2018-06-01|The Federation's map at midsummer 2018}}

The Federation era is the first fully recorded period of Wynncraft guild warfare — the continuous territory-exchange log begins on 3 January 2018, weeks before the era's opening crisis — and it was dominated end to end by a single alliance.

## The Coalition fractures

On 16–17 February 2018, five guilds — [[HackForums]], [[Paladins United]], House of Sentinels, [[Emorians]] and Kangronomicon — left the map-holding [[Coalition]] over map disputes and formed [[Alliance Alliance]] together with [[Fantasy]] and Necronomicon, declaring war on their former allies. In response the Coalition remnant merged with the remains of War Syndicate into a new alliance: the [[the-federation|Federation]], founded and led by [[Drew1011]]. (The founding credit is not undisputed: on 14 November 2018 Slayne posted on the tribute thread, "In a way, you could say that I created Fed because I (along with some others) created Double AA" — a claim to have caused the Federation by co-creating Alliance Alliance, whose split forced the merger. The community record consistently names Drew1011 the founder.) The [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]] ran until 20 March 2018, when the Federation took control of the map.

## Total war, total control

Three days after forming, the Federation attacked HackForums' 111 territories and [[the-wipe-of-hackforums|wiped them to zero in under 12 hours]] on 19 February 2018 — the end of Hax as a territorial power, a year after its ~350-territory peak. From 20 March the Federation held the entire map for 8 months and 25 days, with a single ~3-day interruption in March. A leaderboard capture of 16 April 2018 independently confirms the dominance: all 15 territory holders that day were Federation guilds, 384 territories in total, led by [[Kingdom Foxes]] with 82. The alliance grew to 37–40 member guilds. Within it formed the [[Aesir Pact]] (25 March 2018) — sister guilds Fantasy, Sins of Seedia and IceBlue Team, joined by [[DiamondDeities]] in July, 'especially dedicated to Gavel' — while [[Valkyrie]] persisted alongside as a community layer.

## How the bloc was run

For an alliance of that size the era left almost no constitutional record. What survives is a single line from Drew1011's tribute thanking AurumKitsune of KingdomPhoenixes "for setting up the discord and coming up with things such as the 2/3 majority voting rule that contributed greatly to its success" — a Discord-hosted council of guild leaders deciding by two-thirds majority. Drew1011 also noted that he had "tried to not thank co-leaders and only mention the leaders", which makes the tribute's roll of credited names an approximate register of who sat in that council.

Warfighting was concentrated in a smaller group still. Answering the tribute on 13 November 2018, the member Lego_DW named "the absolute gods of war this alliance created" — himself, 21(n), Goden, _Antho74_, InnerJoker, 0x7cf and snowy — as the people who "really held the alliance together in terms of war power". Goden, a Kingdom Foxes officer who rose from recruit to guild leader inside the era, is the only one of them the corpus places elsewhere.

## Fantasy's war

The era's one sustained challenge came from within. Fantasy left the Federation in late May 2018 and fought it across the map all summer — over 220 territories were exchanged with the bloc — before rejoining on 29 October 2018. The departure date is map-inferred: off-FFA fighting jumps to sustained war levels in the week of 28 May.

## The collapse

At around 3 AM EST on 10 November 2018, one guild left the Federation — and the alliance [[the-federation-dies|cascaded apart within a day]]. The Hive had left a month earlier, then Odysseia; [[Imperial]]'s exit 'snowballed into a major attack on Fed together with the enemy alliance [Ent]'; Arisen followed; and after 14 hours of constant warring the Aesir guilds quit, ending both the Federation and the Aesir Pact. The bracketed tag [Ent] is the only name the era's witnesses gave the opposing bloc, and it corresponds to no alliance otherwise recorded. 'What killed Federation was... internal affairs', wrote Drew1011 in his tribute three days later.

## Aftermath

The winter of 2018–19 was an interregnum: per the community timeline, 'all guilds keep to themselves with valk owning most of Gavel', and exchange data shows Kingdom Foxes and Imperial as the top territory gainers. In the post-collapse chaos [[SOL]] was created — the alliance against which [[Luna]] would form in February 2019, opening [[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]].

## Sources

- 'Federation Tribute' by Drew1011 (Wynncraft forums thread 237070, 13 Nov 2018): roster, founding, duration and death; the 2/3-majority rule credited to AurumKitsune; Lego_DW's war-leader list (post #18); Slayne's claim (page 3, post #45, 14 Nov 2018)
- 'R.i.p Fed' (thread 236962, Nov 2018): the collapse cascade and the [Ent] tag (Ascended Kitten, post #17)
- 'The Aesir Pact' (thread 227373, Jun 2018)
- Community guild-timeline image (imgur seklYAQ, via thread 265297)
- pre2018-territory-snapshots.json (16 Apr 2018 leaderboard capture)
- territory_exchanges map-data analysis (Fantasy's war window; interregnum gains)

articles.title: The private diplomacy era
articles.summary: 2023 to 2026: alliance-making disappeared into private Discords, leaving wars attested only by map data — including the largest wars ever recorded. The record has not reopened: the in-game ally registrations captured from June 2026 document a game mechanic used chiefly to permit joint guild raids, not the era's politics.

infobox.value: [[Avocado Aquarium]] (the era's only named war pact)

infobox.label: Major wars

infobox.value: Diplomacy moved to private Discords and has not returned to the public record

articles.body:
{{map:2024-06-01|The map during the Idiot Co–Aquarium war}}

After [[smtn elf]] faded in mid-2023, something unprecedented happened to the record: it stopped. No alliance roster was published anywhere after June 2022, and from 2023 onward alliance-making happened in private guild Discords. 'Real diplomacy happens in private alliance chats', as [[Titans Valor]]'s founder IceResistance put it; in October 2025 the official Discord's #guild-politics channel was renamed #guild-community. The wars of this era are real and enormous — but their alliances have no recorded names or rosters, and the blocs visible in exchange data cannot be entered into history as anything more than inference.

## The Avocado Aquarium

The era's one named pact is known from testimony and guild artifacts rather than announcements: [[Avocado Aquarium]], the two-guild alliance of [[Avicia]] and [[The Aquarium]] after [[the-avocado-split|they quit smtn elf]] in June 2023, waging a sniping and claim-taking campaign against their former allies into early 2024 and running shared infrastructure including the joint subguild Avoquarium [HQs] (created 9 August 2023). By August 2023 they were each other's 'unwavering ally'. The only other attested relationship of the era is a single September 2023 forum line: 'TNL and AEQ were allied and warring together.'

## Wars known only from the map

Every major war of the era is attested by territory-exchange analysis, not by declarations:

- [[avicia-sequoia-war|Avicia–Sequoia war]] (Oct–Nov 2023, second round Jan 2024) — Avicia against the young [[Sequoia]] (founded 14 Oct 2022), whose rise continued regardless: it won seven consecutive guild seasons from mid-2024.
- [[idiot-co-aquarium-war|Idiot Co–Aquarium war]] (Apr 2024 – Jan 2025) — the biggest war since 2021, peaking at 5,045 quiet-territory exchanges in a week and spanning the 'Rekindled World' map rework of 10 August 2024.
- [[the-long-raid|The Long Raid]] (late Jul – early Aug 2024) — a week-long siege of [[Aequitas]]'s Sky-province claim, the era's only battle with a first-person retelling; the attackers are never named in any surviving text.
- [[aequitas-avicia-war|Aequitas–Avicia war]] (3 Nov – 21 Dec 2025) — the largest war in the entire territory record: 15,710 quiet-territory exchanges, weekly peak 4,736.
- On 25 May 2026 KongoBoys began a sustained campaign against [[Profession Heaven]], ending the neutrality it had held since January 2021.
- [[aequitas-sequoia-war|Aequitas–Sequoia war]] (from Aug 2026, ongoing) — 7,488 quiet-territory exchanges in its first week, with Aequitas driven to zero territories.

## The in-game ally record (2026)

In June 2026 a machine-made record of guild relationships appeared, but not a record of the era's politics. Wynncraft's in-game ally system — present since 2021 — acquired its main practical use when allied guilds gained the ability to run guild raids together, and [[Sequoia]]'s open-source mod began capturing the game's 'formed/revoked an alliance with' broadcasts, producing [[first-machine-recorded-alliances|the first machine-recorded alliances]] (among them a broadcast naming [[GaztheCat]], Sequoia's owner, cancelling an ally registration). From 30 July 2026 the mod auto-snapshots the in-game Diplomacy menu to a private archive (see [[the-diplomacy-update|The Diplomacy update]]).

What became visible is a game-mechanical relationship, used chiefly to permit joint guild raids; it does not indicate political alliance, and guilds registered as in-game allies may be rivals or recent belligerents. The era's paradox therefore stands unresolved: the alliances behind its wars still have no recorded names or rosters, and the public record of who was allied with whom, and why, has not reopened: nothing has succeeded [[the-forum-megalist|the megalist]], whose last roster dates from June 2022.

## Sources

- Wynncraft forums thread 322643 (Oct 2025: #guild-politics renamed) and the IceResistance quotation
- Avicia season posts (threads 308780, 310286); Aequitas thread 280525 p22 (kwiebs, 1 Sep 2023)
- 'Wynncraft Warring – The Long Raid' by Frank Wynncraft (video, premiered 4 Aug 2024) and forums thread 318070
- SequoiaWynncraft/Sequoia-mod repository (commit 69fb472 and the 30 Jul 2026 snapshot feature)
- territory_exchanges map-data analysis (all war windows and volumes)

articles.title: The alliance wars of 2019
articles.summary: The churn year after the Federation's fall: SOL, Luna, Terra, the Council of Canyon Kingdoms and Horologium all rose and collapsed within thirteen months, ending with the disbanding of DiamondDeities in January 2020.
articles.body:
{{map:2019-09-10|The map during the Luna–Terra war}}

No alliance formed in 2019 survived the year intact. Between the [[the-federation-dies|Federation's death]] in November 2018 and the disbanding of [[DiamondDeities]] in January 2020, five successive alliances rose to power and collapsed.

## SOL and the founding of Luna

[[SOL]] was created in the chaos after the Federation's fall in late 2018; its roster was never published and is known only from map-data inference (DiamondDeities, Achte Shadow, Wrath Of Poseidon, Beyond the Scene, Spectral Cabbage, later Ecliptic Awakening). It became the power that [[Luna]] was explicitly formed to counter on 14 February 2019, by [[Imperial]], [[Emorians]], Blacklisted, BuildCraftia and others. Contrary to some retellings, exchange data shows [[Kingdom Foxes]] was not a Luna founder — Luna was at war with Fox from its second day, a war fought across 300+ territories in which Imperial alone attacked Fox 660 times. A leaderboard capture of 3 March 2019 shows the front-runners: Imperial with 85 territories, Emorians with 61. The war ended when Fox joined Luna on 8 July 2019, the day after the Treaty of Ternaves (signed by Fox, [[The Simple Ones]] and ThisIsMurica, splitting the territory of the dissolved Celestial Tigers); the earlier Treaty of Rodoroc (effective 2 March 2019) had already made peace between Fox and DiamondDeities. SOL itself vanishes from the record by mid-2019 as Luna consolidated.

## Luna's map — and Luna's fall

After fending off an attack on Kingdom Foxes, Luna wiped every guild but [[Avicia]]; Avicia joined on 17 July 2019 and Luna held the entire map. Six weeks later it tore itself apart: on 29 August 2019, after a leadership dispute, Emorians and Avicia left and declared war on Imperial, ThisIsMurica was kicked the next day for sending fighters, and [[Terra]] formed in the chaos on 30 August. The war for the map ran 7–19 September — over 2,000 exchanges across 322 territories in ten days. The Simple Ones defected to Terra on 8 September and Terra took map control the same day; Kingdom Foxes left on the 18th and Luna collapsed.

## A participant's account

The year's fullest narrative source is not a forum thread but a memoir chapter, "Recent Wynncraft Guild History", written by [[arkada|Arkada]] — Leonhart_Arkada, an Aedile of [[Titans Valor]] — and published on 14 September 2019, while the fighting was still going on. It is a recollection rather than a record, written by a participant on the Terra side, and its chronology compresses events; but it is the only near-contemporaneous account of the war's politics, and several of its details are corroborated by the map data.

Arkada frames Luna not as a new alliance but as a renamed old one: "The Valkyrie alliance, consisting of Kingdom Foxes, Imperial, Paladins United, and Emorians" crushed a summer raid on Kingdom Foxes, invaded every opposing alliance's land in under two days, and thereafter appears as "the Valkyrie alliance, now calling themselves the Luna alliance". He attributes the raid's failure to Valkyrie's "controversial use of sub guilds", which let main-guild members defend land faster, and records Blacklisted and BuildCraftia defecting to the winning side, then Avicia and The Simple Ones.

His account also supplies a political mechanism for the revolt that broke Luna: the Emorians left "frustrated with the actions of other prominent guilds"; Luna then "seized all of its lands", which he calls "a large mistake", because it made the Emorians sympathetic to the resistance. Terra, in his telling, was a merger of several small anti-Luna alliances — his own guild had been fighting in one called The Ascendancy — that assembled "nearly 15 guilds" for the weekend raid on Imperial and wiped every Luna guild but Kingdom Foxes in about six hours. He closes with a Luna counter-raid on 14 September 2019, forewarned by a spy, which Terra repelled: "Luna could not progress, and we considered their raid a failure." No other source records it.

## Victors without peace

Terra's core founded the [[Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] on 15 September 2019 — Kingdom Foxes, DiamondDeities, Titans Valor, The Simple Ones, [[Fantasy]], Phantom Hearts and Empire of Sindria. On 30 October, Imperial, [[Paladins United]] and Caeruleum Order founded [[Artemis]]. Terra fell on 2 November, seven weeks after its victory, its fragments launching one last raid on the newborn Artemis on 10 November. The Council collapsed on 23 November when The Ascendancy bloc departed. On 1 December, DiamondDeities, Titans Valor and The Simple Ones formed [[Horologium]] — the year's last alliance.

## The end of the churn

On 8 January 2020, [[Nitrogen2Oxygen]] disbanded DiamondDeities, taking Horologium down with it; most remaining members regrouped as Lux Nova the next day. Of the year's combatants only Artemis remained standing — the map-holder of the coming [[artemis-goose-era|Artemis–Goose era]].

- "Inside Myself – Recent Wynncraft Guild History", Wattpad chapter 784189853 by A_Challenger_Arrives (Leonhart_Arkada, Titans Valor), 14 Sep 2019 — near-contemporaneous participant memoir; the Valkyrie→Luna framing, the sub-guild complaint, the Emorians land seizure, Terra's ~15-guild merger and the failed 14 Sep counter-raid

articles.title: The realignment era
articles.summary: May 2021 to mid-2023: Valhalla and Khaos rose from the Great Collapse and fought for a year, Vanir lived twenty days, and the 2022 realignment merged both worlds into Cucumber Company - later smtn elf - until The Aquarium and Avicia walked out in June 2023.
articles.body:
{{map:2022-05-01|The map as Cucumber Company formed}}

The realignment era runs from [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]] of 11 May 2021 to the quiet death of [[smtn elf]] in mid-2023. It began with two blocs at war and ended with nearly all of them in a single super-alliance - and it is the last era with a public alliance record. It is also the first era with a published scoreboard: [[guild-seasons|guild seasons]] launched on 5 July 2021, eight weeks into it, and from then on the map's politics can be read against a table of winners.

## Valhalla and Khaos

On 11 May 2021 thirteen guilds including [[The Aquarium]] formed [[Valhalla]] while nine ex-[[Goose]] guilds formed [[Khaos]], and the [[valhalla-khaos-war|Valhalla-Khaos war]] began the same day. Valhalla took map control within days and dominated the year - 'the meta of being top 10 on the guild sr leaderboard is to join valhalla', a September 2021 forum post complained. Exchange data shows sustained fighting at roughly a thousand exchanges a week at its peaks, continuing into spring 2022.

The season table bears the complaint out only partly. Season 1 (9 Jul - 20 Sep 2021) went to [[ShadowFall]], Season 2 to [[Emorians]], Season 3 to The Aquarium, Season 4 to Nefarious Ravens - four different winners in a year, three of them Valhalla-line guilds and the first of them a guild that had defected from [[Artemis]] to Goose eight months earlier.

## Betrayal and the twenty days of Vanir

In late 2021 The Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes turned on their Valhalla allies - friction visible from August, erupting into open war in December (5,359 quiet-territory exchanges that month). Both were excluded when ten Valhalla guilds reorganized as [[Vanir]] on 28 November 2021. Vanir lasted twenty days: on 18 December [[Emorians]], Nefarious Ravens, IceBlue Team and [[Avicia]] left and it collapsed; [[Niflheim]] officially dissolved the same day. Khaos's war against the ex-Valhalla guilds - its opponents remembered in testimony only as 'the Pineapple Pact', a name with no written record - peaked in January 2022 at 500-800 quiet-territory exchanges per week and faded to nothing by mid-July.

## Cucumber Company and smtn elf

The 2022 realignment merged the ex-Valhalla and ex-Khaos worlds into [[Cucumber Company]], formed for guild Season 5 - 'our first season being a part of the new Cucumber Company war alliance', wrote [[titan-times|Titan Times]]. Season 5 ran from 3 March to 2 May 2022; earlier chronicle drafts approximated the Cucumber joins to a 1 April season start, and the season table corrects that to 3 March. Its 14-guild roster, posted to [[the-forum-megalist|the forum megalist]] on 26 June 2022, was the last public alliance roster ever; the megalist's alliance section was deleted twelve days later. At the start of Season 8, which began on 12 September 2022, 'Cucumber was archived. The new alliance name is called Smtn else' - the same newsletter recording Gang of Fools having 'left and betrayed the alliance' and welcoming [[Paladins United]], [[The Simple Ones]] and TerraLune. Renamed 'smtn elf' for Christmas 2022 and never changed back, the super-alliance was crowned - satirically - 'unquestionably the greatest super-alliance of 2023' that February. In spring 2023 busted moments and [[Idiot Co]] joined. Meanwhile the community layer turned over: as [[Hestia]] declined, the leaders of [[Titans Valor]] and Empire of Sindria founded [[Adonis]] around May 2022 as its effective successor.

Under the super-alliance the crown circulated among its own members - The Aquarium in Season 5, KongoBoys in Season 6, [[Avicia]] in Season 7, The Aquarium again in Season 8 - and then stopped circulating. Avicia won Seasons 9 through 13 without a break, from October 2022 to August 2023, a run that begins inside smtn elf and ends after it.

## The Eden coup

Somewhere in this period [[Eden]], a founding guild of Khaos, was overthrown from within. The entire public record of the event is one sentence in a guild application to [[Titans Valor]], written by a player called xK6TA and quoted in post #1922 of the ANO recruitment thread on 16 April 2023: 'I was a part of Eden when it was #1 and slightly after it got couped.' No other source mentions it - not Eden's own thread, not the megalist, not Titan Times. The coup's actors are unrecorded, its date only bounded above by April 2023, and the sense of '#1' unexplained, since Eden never won a guild season.

## The end

In June 2023 The Aquarium and Avicia quit smtn elf, rejecting pressure to shrink their claims, and opened [[the-avocado-split|the Avocado split]] against their former allies. smtn elf's last recorded mention is Avicia's season post of 10 June 2023 - the closing days of the Season 12 it had won; by the next season post it had vanished from the record, with no death announcement, just silence. With it ended the era of publicly named alliances, and [[private-diplomacy-era|the private diplomacy era]] began.

## Sources

- Wynncraft forums thread 278112 ('the megalist'), posts of 25 May 2021 (the Valhalla/Khaos renames), 7 Jul 2021 and 26 Jun 2022 (the Cucumber Company roster; deletion 7 Jul 2022)
- Wynncraft forums thread 295680 (IamFye, 25 Sep 2021) on Valhalla's dominance
- Wynncraft forums thread 206094 p97, post #1922 (16 Apr 2023): xK6TA's application, the sole record of the Eden coup
- Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guild Seasons': season dates and winners for Seasons 1-13
- Titan Times vols. 1 (8 May 2022), 3 (12 Jun 2022), 6 (12 Oct 2022) and 9 (25 Mar 2023)
- Avicia season posts (threads 308780 of 10 Jun 2023 and 310286 of 19 Aug 2023)
- Cameron (TAq veteran) oral testimony, fact-checked against map data (the betrayal; the Christmas rename)
- territory_exchanges map-data analysis (war volumes and windows)

articles.title: Adonis
articles.summary: Adonis was a community alliance founded around May 2022 by the leaders of Titans Valor and Empire of Sindria as Hestia declined — 'a space for those of us who are still active to hang together.' Joined by Avicia within weeks, it outlived the war alliances around it, still hosting community events in early 2024.
articles.body:
**Adonis** was a community alliance founded around May 2022 by the leaders of [[Titans Valor]] and Empire of Sindria as [[Hestia]] declined — in the words of Titans Valor's newsletter, “a space for those of us who are still active to hang together.” It outlived every war alliance around it.

## History
[[titan-times|Titan Times]] vol. 1 (8 May 2022) records the founding, framing Adonis as the successor to the declining Hestia; [[Avicia]] had joined by vol. 3 (12 June 2022). The alliance ran community events through the era of [[Cucumber Company]], [[smtn elf]] and the [[Avocado Aquarium]] — its member guilds passing through those war blocs while Adonis held the social layer, exactly as Hestia had spanned the war blocs before it.

Titan Times vol. 12 (20 February 2024) still records Adonis community events, and vol. 13 (22 March 2024) a joint Discord server run with the guild The Farplane (whose membership status in Adonis is unclear from the source and is not entered in the chronicle). That March 2024 issue is the alliance's last attestation; no dissolution was ever recorded.

## Membership
The end date marks last attestation, not a recorded dissolution.

{{alliance:Adonis}}

## Legacy
Adonis carried the community-alliance tradition of [[Hestia]] and [[Niflheim]] into the mid-2020s, and demonstrated its durability: while the war alliances of 2022–2023 collapsed or faded within a season or two, Adonis was still hosting events nearly two years after its founding — the last attested alliance of the community layer.

## Sources
- Titan Times vol. 1 (8 May 2022), vol. 3 (12 Jun 2022), vol. 12 (20 Feb 2024) and vol. 13 (22 Mar 2024)

articles.title: Aesir Pact
articles.summary: The Aesir Pact was a 2018 pact of sister guilds inside the Federation, "especially dedicated to Gavel, and the birth place of Aesir, the canyon." Created on 25 Mar 2018 by Fantasy, Sins of Seedia and IceBlue Team, its guilds were the Federation's last defenders, and Aesir died with it on 10–11 Nov 2018.

articles.body:
The **Aesir Pact** (tag **Aesir**) was a pact of sister guilds inside [[the-federation|the Federation]] in 2018, "especially dedicated to Gavel, and the birth place of Aesir, the canyon." Its guilds were the Federation's last defenders, and Aesir died with it in November 2018.

## History

### Formation
The pact was created on 25 Mar 2018 by [[Fantasy]], Sins of Seedia and IceBlue Team as a bond of sister guilds within the map-dominant Federation. [[DiamondDeities]] was accepted into the pact on 18 Jul 2018. Its public thread, posted by the Sins of Seedia leader lotuss on 5 Jun 2018 and last edited on 21 Jul 2018, describes Aesir as "an alliance, or if you will sister-ship pact, between 4 warring and growing community guilds" and gives the pact's own origin story: Fantasy and Sins of Seedia became friends during the War Syndicate era, were separated when Fantasy entered the [[Coalition]] and Sins of Seedia warred against it, and were reunited inside the Federation, where IceBlue Team and then DiamondDeities were added.

### Leadership
The thread names two leaders for each member guild — the fullest leadership roster recorded for any 2018 sub-alliance.

| Guild | Tag | Leaders |
|---|---|---|
| [[Fantasy]] | Fux | [[viaire|Viaire]], SpaseCow |
| Sins of Seedia | SDU | [[simplyinfinity|simplyinfinity_]], Shy_Phoenix |
| IceBlue Team | IBT | [[vmark03|Vmark03]], Mpr100 |
| [[DiamondDeities]] | DDT | [[nitrogen2oxygen|Nitrogen2Oxygen]], Icey_Diamond |

New guilds were admitted by a vote of these leaders; the thread advised applicants to form friendships with them first, "for (voting process)". Several of the same names recur in the Federation's own leadership record: simplyinfinity_ is credited by [[Drew1011]] as the first to accept the merger proposal that created the Federation, Viaire as "perhaps the best mapmaker the alliance had", and Nitrogen2Oxygen and Icey_Diamond as its most trusted friends.

### The Fantasy anomaly
The record preserves an oddity no source resolves: Fantasy was an Aesir founder, yet waged war on the Federation itself from May to October 2018, a conflict attested in map data with more than 220 territories exchanged. The pact evidently survived Fantasy's exit from the Federation — the chronicle records Fantasy's Aesir membership as unbroken from the founding to the end.

### The last defence
When the Federation began to cascade apart on 10 Nov 2018, the Aesir guilds — Sins of Seedia, DiamondDeities and IceBlue Team — were its last defenders, quitting only after 14 hours of constant warring as [[the-federation-dies|the Federation fell]] on 10–11 Nov 2018. The community timeline records simply: "At this point Aesir died too."

## Membership
{{alliance:Aesir Pact}}

## Legacy
The pact never existed apart from the Federation: it formed inside the bloc and ended at the hour of its fall. Its guilds scattered into the post-Federation world — DiamondDeities into [[SOL]] within weeks, while IceBlue Team and Fantasy resurfaced in [[Terra]] during the wars of 2019.

## Sources
- "The Aesir Pact", Wynncraft forums thread 227373 (lotuss, 5 Jun 2018, last edited 21 Jul 2018) — the four-guild leader table, the origin story, the voting process; DiamondDeities' acceptance recorded 18 Jul 2018
- "Federation Tribute", Wynncraft forums thread 237070 (Drew1011, 13 Nov 2018) — the Federation-side credits for simplyinfinity_, Viaire, Nitrogen2Oxygen, Icey_Diamond and ItzVmark03
- "R.i.p Fed", Wynncraft forums thread 236962 (Nov 2018) — the 14-hour last defence
- Community guild-timeline image (imgur seklYAQ), via thread 265297 — founding date; "At this point Aesir died too"
- Community Timeline document; territory_exchanges map-data analysis (the Fantasy–Federation war)

articles.title: Alliance Alliance
articles.summary: Alliance Alliance ("Double AA") was the breakaway war alliance of February 2018: five guilds that split from the Coalition over map disputes, joined by Fantasy and Necronomicon. Its month-long rebellion — the Coalition Civil War — ended when the newly formed Federation took the entire map on 20 Mar 2018.
articles.body:
**Alliance Alliance** (tag **AA**; "Double AA" in one participant's telling) was a short-lived Wynncraft war alliance of February–March 2018 — the five guilds that split from the [[Coalition]], joined by two allies, whose rebellion triggered the creation of [[the-federation|the Federation]].

## History

### Formation
On 17 Feb 2018 (the community guild-timeline image dates the split a day earlier), [[HackForums]], [[Paladins United]], House of Sentinels, [[Emorians]] and Kangronomicon left the Coalition — "The 1st Coalition" in the Timeline document — over map disputes. Together with [[Fantasy]] and Necronomicon they formed Alliance Alliance and declared war on their former alliance, beginning the [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]]. (The Timeline document spells the seventh guild "Necromonicon"; the chronicle resolves it to Necronomicon, a guild active on the map through 2018.)

### The Coalition Civil War
The war set Alliance Alliance against the Coalition remnant, which had merged with War Syndicate's remains into the new Federation. The Federation struck first and hardest: three days after forming, it attacked member guild HackForums' 111 territories and [[the-wipe-of-hackforums|wiped them to zero]] in under 12 hours, ending HackForums as a territorial power. The war ended on 20 Mar 2018 when the Federation took control of the entire map.

No formal dissolution of Alliance Alliance was ever recorded. The chronicle closes its member stints on 19–20 Mar 2018, when the bloc was absorbed: Fantasy, Paladins United and Emorians all appear on the Federation's rolls from that date.

## Membership
{{alliance:Alliance Alliance}}

## Legacy
Alliance Alliance existed for barely a month, but its split ended the Coalition and provoked the merger that created the Federation, the alliance that dominated the rest of 2018 (the [[federation-era|Federation era]]). One participant, Slayne, later tied the Federation's creation directly to it: "I created Fed because I (along with some others) created Double AA" (2018 — the statement is preserved in the chronicle's research notes; its original thread is not recorded).

## Sources

- Community guild-timeline image (imgur seklYAQ), via Wynncraft forums thread 265297 — the 16 Feb dating
- Slayne's 2018 "Double AA" statement, preserved in the chronicle's 2018-era research notes (original thread unrecorded)
